    The script is a comedic dialogue between Nathan Fielder, the main character of the TV show "Nathan for You," and Joe, the owner of a deli. Nathan proposes an idea to Joe to create a massive sandwich called the "Goliath Sandwich" that will attract customers and make the deli famous. The sandwich will be so large that it will be a challenge for customers to finish it, and if they succeed, their name will be put on a plaque on the wall of fame.

    * Start with an introduction where Nathan introduces himself to Joe and explains that he is there to help improve his deli business.
    * Nathan asks Joe about his deli and what sets it apart from others in the area.
    * Joe explains that they have a great selection of sandwiches and deli meats, and a loyal customer base.
    * Nathan proposes the idea of creating the Goliath Sandwich, which will be a massive sandwich made with every single meat and cheese in the deli, plus all the toppings and condiments.
    * Joe is hesitant at first, but Nathan convinces him that it will be a great way to attract attention to the deli.
    * Nathan explains that the challenge will be to finish the sandwich within one hour, and if customers succeed, they will get the sandwich for free and their name will be put on a plaque on the wall of fame.
    * Joe agrees to go ahead with the idea, and Nathan starts making the Goliath Sandwich.
    * The script ends with a narrator asking if anyone will be able to conquer the Goliath Sandwich and claim their place on the wall of fame, and inviting viewers to tune in to find out on "Nathan for You."

1955603320212684834 [2025-08-13] @fchollet 💜 6627 🔁 1248
GenAI isn't just a technology; it's an informational pollutant—a pervasive cognitive smog that touches and corrupts every aspect of the Internet. It's not just a productivity tool; it's a kind of digital acid rain, silently eroding the value of all information.

Every image is no longer a glimpse of reality, but a potential vector for synthetic deception. Every article is no longer a unique voice, but a soulless permutation of data, a hollow echo in the digital chamber. This isn't just content creation; it's the flattening of the entire vibrant ecosystem of human expression, transforming a rich tapestry of ideas into a uniform, gray slurry of derivative, algorithmically optimized outputs.

This isn't just innovation; it's the systematic contamination of our data streams, a semantic sludge that clogs the channels of genuine communication and cheapens the value of human thought—leaving us to sift through a digital landfill for a single original idea.

rating.reasoning_summary: This strand tracks the evolution of AI-generated comedy from 2021 concept jokes through 2023's experimental 'infinite sitcom' streams to 2025's debates about whether AI can actually be funny. The boundary object shifts from philosophical humor (Rortian/Peirciean joke) to GPT-generated absurdist scripts, then to viral AI video memes, culminating in the Golden Gate Claude incident—an AI model that became unintentionally hilarious by injecting the Golden Gate Bridge into every topic including the Rwandan genocide. The discourse is constructive (exploring AI's comedic potential) until fchollet's 2025 critique reframes GenAI as 'informational pollutant,' which itself becomes a meta-joke when accused of being AI-written. Low evolution: the idea remains 'can AI be funny?' throughout, with examples accumulating but no conceptual refinement.

essential_tweets.annotation: The origin: Philosophy humor as human baseline for wit
First GPT comedy experiment: Nathan For You script generation
The 'Infinite Sitcom' era: AI-generated Simpsons/Seinfeld streams
GPT-4 as 'absurdist standup': the talking egg problem
Viral moment: 'If Snapchat existed back then' AI video genre
The tonal shift: GPT-4o becomes 'overly enthusiastic 1990s teenager'
Provocative claim: AI comedians will replace human standups
The Golden Gate Claude incident: peak unintentional AI comedy
The backlash: fchollet's 'GenAI as informational pollutant' manifesto
Meta-closure: Human declares their AI-sounding critique is 'parody'
